item.title: Understanding the Warranty on Taylor Machines
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
When investing in a Taylor machine, it comes along with a robust warranty package with your purchase. Taylor Products is committed to providing high-quality, reliable equipment, and our warranty reflects that commitment. Here's a breakdown of what you can expect in terms of warranty coverage for both new and used Taylor machines.

Warranty for New Taylor Models

For new Taylor models, we offer a comprehensive warranty package designed to ensure your machine operates smoothly and efficiently for years to come:

1 Year Service: We provide one year of service coverage, ensuring that any issues, other than operational parts, are promptly addressed by our expert technicians.

1 Year Parts: All parts are covered for the first year, other than operational parts, so if anything needs to be replaced, it’s taken care of at no cost to you.

2 Year Motors & Gear Boxes: The motors and gearboxes in our machines are built to last, and we back this with a two-year warranty, giving you peace of mind.

5 Year Refrigeration Compressor: The refrigeration compressor is vital to your machine’s cooling capabilities, and we provide a five-year warranty to ensure it stays in top working condition.

5 Year Insulated Shell Assembly: The insulated shell assembly, which helps maintain the machine's efficiency and performance, is covered for five years, ensuring long-term reliability.

Warranty for Used Taylor Machines

We also offer solid warranty coverage for used Taylor machines, making them a reliable choice for businesses looking to optimize their budget. We replace all wearable parts, test and replace any parts that are not up to spec:

1 Year Service: Even with a used machine, you’ll benefit from one year of service coverage, other than operational parts, so any necessary repairs are handled by our trained technicians.

1 Year Parts: Used Taylor machines come with a one-year parts warranty, so you’re protected if any part, other than operational parts, needs to be replaced during the first year of operation.

Compressor and Shell Assembly: Used Taylor machines come with up to a 3 year compressor and shell assembly warranty, depending on the age.

Wearable Parts Exclusion

Please be aware that class 000 parts, such as blades, O-rings, and other wearable components, are not included in the warranty coverage. These parts are subject to regular wear and tear and will need to be replaced periodically as part of standard maintenance.

Conclusion

Taylor Products stands by the quality of our machines, offering robust warranty options for both new and used models. Whether you're purchasing a brand-new Taylor machine or opting for a used one, you can rest assured that you're getting a product that's backed by comprehensive service and parts coverage. item.title: Essential Maintenance Tips for Your Taylor Machine [And Winterization]
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Proper maintenance of your Taylor machine is vital to ensuring its long-term performance and reliability. Regular maintenance not only extends the lifespan of your equipment but also helps you avoid costly repairs and downtime. Here are the key maintenance tasks recommended by Taylor Company every 90 days to keep your machine running smoothly.

Taylor Company's 90-Day Maintenance Recommendations

To keep your Taylor machine in optimal condition, the following maintenance tasks should be performed every 90 days:

Replace Scraper Blades:

Scraper blades wear down over time and can affect the quality of your frozen products. Replacing them regularly ensures that your machine continues to operate efficiently.

Use a Tune-Up Kit:

The tune-up kit includes essential components like O-rings, drive shaft seals, door gaskets, and front bearings. Replacing these parts helps maintain the integrity of your machine’s internal components.

Pump Tune-Up Kits:

Depending on your machine model, you might need a simplified kit or a Co-Ax kit for pump maintenance. These kits include all necessary parts to keep your pump functioning correctly.

How to Identify the Correct Part Numbers

Knowing the correct part numbers is crucial for ordering the right components for your Taylor machine. Here are some tips on how to identify the parts you need:

Check the Operator’s Manual:

Your machine’s operator manual is the first place to look for part numbers and maintenance instructions. It provides detailed information specific to your model.

Log in to Our Parts Website:

Visit parts.taylorproducts.net to log in or request access. Our website lists all operator parts, making it easy to find what you need.

Contact Parts Support:

If you’re unsure about which parts to order, our parts support team is here to help. Call us at 800-633-1157 or email parts@taylorproducts.net for personalized assistance.

Special Considerations for Water-Cooled Freezers

If you have a water-cooled freezer stored in a non-heated area, it’s essential to winterize it to prevent damage during cold weather. We offer professional winterization services by certified technicians, and this service is highly recommended to protect your equipment.

Regular maintenance is vital to keeping your Taylor machine in top working condition. By following these 90-day maintenance recommendations, you can ensure your machine operates efficiently and produces high-quality products consistently. Whether you need parts, maintenance kits, or professional services, Taylor Products is here to support you. For any questions or to order parts, contact us today or visit our parts website.

item.title: How Much Electricity Does a Taylor Machine Use Per Day?
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Understanding the electricity usage of your Taylor machine is crucial for managing your operational costs. Here’s a simple breakdown of how much electricity a typical Taylor machine might use:

Daily Electricity Consumption

Power Requirements: 20 Amp x 208V = 4,160 Watts
Daily Usage: 4,160 Watts x 12 hours a day = 49,920 Watts
Converted to Kilowatts: 49,920 / 1,000 = 49.92 kWh

Cost Calculation*

Cost per Day: 49.92 kWh x 14.83 cents (NJ average kWh cost for commercial customers) = $7.40 per day
Cost per Month: $7.40 x 30 days = $222 per month

This calculation shows that a typical Taylor machine would cost approximately $222 per month to operate, based on average usage and electricity rates. This is an essential factor to consider when planning your operational budget, especially for businesses looking to manage energy costs effectively.

*Cost calculation is based on assumptions for electricity costs. Your costs may vary. Contact your electric supplier for more details and information.

item.title: Create Flavors For The Fall Season
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Did you know that you can add flavor compounds to both dairy and non-dairy bases to create artisan soft serve flavors perfect for any season? Whether you run a pumpkin patch farm stand or an ice cream shop, you can easily craft exciting new treats. With just a soft serve base and a whisk, the possibilities are endless!

Seasonal Treat: Pumpkin Soft Serve Ice Cream

Pumpkin soft serve ice cream is a fall favorite that blends the smooth, creamy texture of traditional soft serve with the warm spices of pumpkin pie. Imagine a rich, creamy base with hints of cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves, giving each bite the nostalgic taste of autumn. Whether in a cone or cup, this seasonal delight can be topped with a sprinkle of cinnamon for an extra flavor boost.

Comfort Food at its Best: Chai Tea Soft Serve

For something a little different, try chai tea soft serve. Inspired by the aromatic and spiced chai tea from India, this soft serve is both energizing and soothing. With a base of black tea and spices like cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and ginger, chai soft serve offers a warm, spicy flavor profile that’s perfect for cool weather and pairs well with fall’s crisp air.

Crisp and Sweet: Apple Cider Soft Serve

Nothing says fall like apple cider! Apple soft serve combines the velvety texture of soft serve with the tangy sweetness of apples. Reminiscent of apple pie or cider, this frozen treat can be made with tart green apple or sweet red apple flavors. Top it off with a drizzle of homemade caramel sauce for an irresistible dessert that will leave your customers craving more.

Recipe Highlight: Homemade Caramel Sauc

For those looking to add an extra indulgent touch to their soft serve, homemade caramel sauce is the perfect complement. Here’s how to make it:

Ingredients:

  • 1 cup granulated sugar
  • 6 tablespoons unsalted butter (cut into pieces)
  • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • 1/4 teaspoon sea salt (optional for salted caramel)

Instructions:

  1. Prepare Ingredients: Have your butter and cream ready before starting.
  2. Heat the Sugar: In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, melt the sugar over medium heat, stirring constantly.
  3. Caramelize the Sugar: Once melted, the sugar will turn a deep amber color. Be careful not to burn it.
  4. Add Butter: Carefully stir in the butter—watch out for bubbling!
  5. Incorporate Cream: Slowly pour in the cream while stirring. The caramel will bubble again.
  6. Season: Add sea salt if desired. Stir until smooth.
  7. Cool & Store: Let the caramel cool before storing in an airtight container.

Tips:

  • Keep a close eye on the sugar to prevent burning.
  • Stir constantly to avoid scorching.
  • Soak any hardened caramel in warm water for easy clean-up.

Contact Us for Recipe and Menu Ideas

Whether you're crafting pumpkin soft serve, chai tea soft serve, or apple cider flavors, Taylor Products has everything you need to make your seasonal menu shine. Contact us today for flavor ideas, recipes, and guidance on how to create your next best-selling artisan soft serve!

item.title: Why Is My Ice Cream Soft?
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Overbeaten soft serve is a common issue that can affect the texture, consistency, and overall quality of your frozen treats. But what exactly is overbeaten soft serve, and how can it be avoided?

What is Overbeaten Soft Serve?

Overbeaten soft serve occurs when the product loses some of its air content, known as "overrun." Overrun refers to the amount of air that is incorporated into the ice cream during the freezing process, which gives soft serve its light, creamy texture. The ideal overrun for soft serve typically falls between 35% and 60%, ensuring the best quality and appearance.

When the overrun drops too low, the soft serve becomes dense and lacks its signature airy, smooth feel. This often happens when the product sits in the freezing cylinder for too long while it’s being dispensed, leading to an overbeaten texture.

Mechanical Issues Leading to Soft, Overbeaten Soft Serve

There are several mechanical reasons why your soft serve machine might produce overbeaten product. Here are some of the most common causes:

1. Worn Scraper Blades:
Worn-out scraper blades can prevent the soft serve from being efficiently scraped off the freezing cylinder, which causes insulation between the product and the freezing surface. This results in the product spinning too long in the cylinder, leading to overbeating.

2. Viscosity Setting Too High:
If the viscosity setting is too high, the refrigeration and beater motor may run continuously without cycling off. This prolonged operation can cause the product to overbeat, affecting the texture and quality of the soft serve.

3. Low Refrigerant Charge:
A soft serve machine running low on refrigerant may struggle to maintain the proper temperature, leading to soft or improperly frozen product. This can result in the soft serve being overbeaten due to longer freezing times.

4. High Ambient Temperatures for Air-Cooled Freezers:
Air-cooled freezers operating in high ambient temperatures can overheat and fail to freeze the product effectively, which can also cause overbeaten soft serve. Ensuring the machine is in a well-ventilated area with proper air circulation can help prevent this issue.

5. Gravity-Fed Machine Mix Air Tube Not Flipped To Standby Overnight

Be sure to turn the mix feed tube in the standby position with the hole at the top. This keeps the air in the barrel overnight. When turning on AUTO, the product will be airy, not heavy and wet.

By addressing these mechanical issues and maintaining your soft serve machine properly, you can avoid producing overbeaten product and ensure a consistently high-quality soft serve experience for your customers.

item.title: What Kind of Soft Serve Machine is Right for Me?
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Choosing the perfect soft serve machine for your business is crucial for smooth operations and customer satisfaction. At Taylor Products, we guide you through key considerations to help you make the best choice for your needs. Here's what to think about when selecting a machine:

1. Menu Offerings

Your menu plays a significant role in determining the machine capacity you'll need.

  • High Capacity Machines: If your menu includes shakes, ice cream cakes, or larger items, a mid to high-capacity machine is essential. These machines can handle larger serving sizes efficiently.
  • Medium to Low Capacity Machines: For businesses focused on cones and cups, lower or medium capacity machines should suffice. These machines are ideal for smaller portions and lighter traffic.

2. Sales Volume

Understanding your daily and hourly sales patterns will help determine the capacity of your machine.

  • Consistent Sales Over Time: If you’re selling 30 items over 8-10 hours, a lower capacity machine may work well.
  • High-Volume Periods: For stores that sell the 100 items within 3 hours, a higher output capacity is necessary to meet peak demand without long wait times.

3. Electrical Requirements

Ensure your business can support the electrical needs of the machine you choose.

  • 120 Volts: Ideal for low-capacity machines.
  • 208-230 Volts: Suited for mid to high-capacity machines.
  • 1 Phase (3 wire): Common in most buildings.
  • 3 Phase (4 wire): Check 3 Phase availability in your building or store.

4. Cooling Options

All of our Taylor Products machines are available in in Air-Cooled options. Most medium- and high-volume machines are available in Water-Cooled options.

  • Air-Cooled Machines: These machines use an internal blower to cool the system and are easier to install.
  • Water-Cooled Machines: These require a ½” cold water line, a ¾” shut-off valve, and a forced drain within 5 feet of the machine.

5. Machine Styles

The style of your soft serve machine can vary based on the flavors you offer and the space you have available.

item.title: Understanding Overrun in Shakes and Soft Serve [With Calculator]
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to creating the perfect shake or soft serve, achieving the right texture is key—and overrun plays a significant role in that. Overrun refers to the amount of air incorporated into a shake or soft serve mix during the freezing process, which makes the product lighter, fluffier, and gives it that classic creamy texture we all love.

In simple terms, overrun is the increase in the volume of the mix due to the air that’s added during freezing. It’s typically expressed as a percentage, and understanding how to calculate overrun is important for the best-tasting product and controlling food costs.

How to Calculate Overrun for Shakes and Soft Serve

Calculating overrun is a straightforward process that can help you assess the quality and consistency of your shake or soft serve. Follow these steps to determine the overrun percentage:

  1. Measure the Volume of the Mix (Y): Before incorporating air, measure the volume of your raw shake or soft serve mix. For example, if you have 15 oz of mix, that’s your starting point.
  2. Measure the Volume of the Finished Product (X): After blending or freezing, measure the final volume of the shake or soft serve with the air incorporated. Suppose the volume now measures 10 oz.
  3. Calculate the Difference: Subtract the initial volume (Y) from the final volume (X).
  4. Divide by the Initial Volume: Divide the difference by the initial volume of the mix.
  5. Multiply by 100: Multiply the result by 100 to get the overrun percentage.

In this example, the overrun is 33%, meaning that 33% of the final product's volume is air, which gives it that light and fluffy texture.

Why Is Overrun Important?

The right amount of overrun affects the texture, mouthfeel, and even the taste of your product. If there’s too little air, your soft serve or shake may end up dense and heavy, while too much air can make it too light and possibly dilute the flavor. Ideally, the overrun for soft serve should range between 35% and 60% for optimal quality and consistency.

Need Help Perfecting Your Overrun?

If you need guidance on achieving the perfect overrun for your shakes or soft serve, or if you're looking for the right equipment to maintain consistency, reach out to Taylor Products. Our team can help you fine-tune your process for top-notch results every time.

item.title: How to Test Soft Serve Mix Viscosity [Homemade & Plant-Based]
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
To ensure your Taylor soft serve machine is running efficiently and producing the highest quality product, it's important to regularly test the viscosity of your mix. Below are instructions on how to test the viscosity for both gravity-style and pump-style Taylor freezers.

How to Test Mix Viscosity: Gravity Style Freezers

Prime the Freezer:

  • Sanitize your Taylor freezer thoroughly.
  • Fill the hopper halfway or more with your soft serve mix.

Prepare for Testing:

  • Insert the mix tube into the "Auto" position.
  • Place the air orifice on the tube, but do not turn the Taylor machine on yet.
  • Ensure the draw handle opens fully. Some handles may have a draw rate adjustment screw that can be fine-tuned later.

Required Tools:

  • A scale.
  • A 12–20 oz cup.

Test the Draw Rate:

  • Open the handle fully and observe the flow of the mix:
    • If the mix flows freely in a steady stream, the viscosity is correct.
    • If the product drips or stops flowing, check if the handle is opening fully.
    • If the mix does not flow freely, STOP. Reformulate the mix. Do not turn the machine to "AUTO" as this could cause mechanical issues.

Measure Viscosity:

  • Keep the freezer off and open the draw handle to dispense the unfrozen mix into the cup for 10 seconds.
  • Weigh the dispensed product. The target flow rate is 8-10 oz within those 10 seconds.

How to Test Mix Viscosity: Pump Style Freezers

Prime the Freezer:

  • Sanitize the Taylor pump-style freezer and fill the hopper halfway with your mix.

Prepare for Testing:

  • Install the mix pump but leave the mix feed tube detached from the barrel.
  • Turn on the mix pump. If the mix flows freely, you’re ready to proceed. If it doesn’t, the mix may be too thick. STOP and reformulate the mix.

Test Pump Flow:

  • Place a cup under the pump's discharge port to catch the mix. Run the pump for five cycles.
  • Weigh the mix. The amount dispensed should weigh at least 5 ounces. If it is, the viscosity is correct. If less than 5 ounces, reformulate the mix.

item.title: How to Install a Taylor Machine/Freezer
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Installing a Taylor machine or freezer is straightforward if you follow the proper steps and have the right setup. This guide will walk you through the key elements to ensure a smooth installation.
Note: Freezers should be moved by a professional due to the weight, to avoid any injuries.

Before installation, confirm data plate information to assure correct electrical and cooling configurations.

  • All purchases from Taylor Products include specific requirements noted on the sales order. For questions about your machine’s specifications, consult:
    • Your Salesman: Meet Your Salesman

Step 2: Electrical Configurations

Taylor machines require specific electrical setups. Below are the most common configurations:

  • 120 Volt
    • 15 or 20 Amps
    • Wire size: 12-gauge copper wire
  • 208-230/60/3Ph
    • 20 Amp: Wire size 12-gauge copper wire
    • 30 Amp: Wire size 10-gauge copper wire
  • 208-230/60/1Ph
    • 20 Amp: Wire size 12-gauge copper wire
    • 30 Amp: Wire size 10-gauge copper wire

Taylor Products machines use twist-lock receptacles for 208-230 V models.

Electrical Notes:

  • Water Usage: These machines can use up to ¾ gallon of water per minute under full load. They are not recommended for locations with private wells or septic systems.

item.title: Air-Cooled vs. Water-Cooled Taylor Machines: Making the Right Choice
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
When investing in a Taylor soft serve machine, one critical decision is choosing between air-cooled and water-cooled models. Each cooling system has distinct advantages and considerations. Here's a breakdown to assist you in making an informed choice:

Air-Cooled Machines

Advantages:

  • No Water Supply Needed: Air-cooled machines dissipate heat using ambient air, eliminating the need for a water connection.
  • Flexible Installation: Without plumbing requirements, these machines offer more versatility in placement within your establishment.

Considerations:

  • Ambient Temperature Sensitivity: Hot environments may reduce efficiency, strain other equipment and AC units
  • Heat Dispersion: They release warm air into the room, potentially impacting the comfort of your workspace.

Water-Cooled Machines

Advantages:

  • Water Cooling: Water-cooled systems run quieter and don’t give off heat into the stores space.
  • Stable Performance: Less influenced by ambient temperatures, making them suitable for warmer climates or confined spaces.

Considerations:

  • Water Usage: These machines generally can use ¾ gallon of water per minute under full load. They need a good cool water supply source, raise environmental concerns in some towns. Not recommended for well water supply.
  • Installation Requirements: Access to plumbing is necessary ¾ inch GHT cold water with shut off and forced drain.

Making the Choice

Your decision should align with your business's operational environment and priorities. If water costs are a concern or plumbing access is limited, an air-cooled machine may be more practical.

Conclusion

Both air-cooled and water-cooled Taylor machines are designed to deliver exceptional performance. Assessing your establishment's specific needs and constraints will guide you to the cooling system that best supports your business objectives.

item.title: Gravity-Fed vs. Pump - Pressurized Taylor Machines
item.dc:creator: adventiimedia
item.content:encoded:
Gravity-Fed Machines

Gravity-fed machines rely on gravity to move the mix from the hopper to the freezing cylinder using a mix feed tube and air orifice.

Overrun Characteristics:

  • Consistent Overrun: Typically achieves around 30-40% overrun, resulting in a denser product.
  • Simplicity and Reliability: Fewer mechanical components mean easier maintenance and operation.

Example: The Taylor C713 is one of our twin-twist, gravity-fed machine, ideal for businesses seeking a high volume operation with consistent product quality.

Pump-Pressurized Machines

Pump-Pressurized  models use pumps to deliver the mix to the freezing cylinder under pressure, allowing for greater % of overrun. Overrun can range from 30% to 80% typically.

Pump style overrun cab be adjusted by changing the pump valve cap in our simplified pump or valve body in our co-ax pump.

Overrun Characteristics:

  • Adjustable Overrun: Capable of achieving 25-80% overrun, offering flexibility to produce lighter, airier products or denser treats based on customer preference.
  • Enhanced Texture Control: Allows for precise manipulation of product texture and mouthfeel.

Example: The Taylor C716 28HT is a Pump-Pressurized machine designed for high-volume establishments and adjustable overrun settings.

Making the Choice

Your decision between gravity-fed and Pump-Pressurized machines should align with your business model and taste preferences. If your clientele favors a richer, denser soft serve, a gravity-fed machine may be suitable. Conversely, if a lighter texture and higher yield are desired, a pump-fed machine would be advantageous.

Conclusion

Understanding the differences between gravity-fed and Pump-Pressurized Taylor machines is essential for delivering the desired soft serve experience. By considering factors such as overrun, texture, and operational requirements, you can select the machine that best aligns with your business objectives and delights your customers.

Icetro ISI-271: Effortless Self-Service Soft Serve

Introducing the Icetro ISI-271—fully automated self-service soft serve at the touch of a button! Whether your customers prefer cones or cups*, the ISI-271 simplifies serving by dispensing perfect portions every single time, automatically.

Beyond its convenience, the ISI-271 features advanced heat treatment technology that significantly extends cleaning intervals. This means fewer interruptions and more uptime for your business. To make your life even easier, Taylor Products offers the exclusive Brush Butler regular cleaning program, so you can say goodbye to cleaning hassles and hello to consistently smooth operations.

Frozen Beverages with Flavorburst Syrup Options

Everyone loves the classic taste of lemonade or the timeless blend of lemonade iced tea. Now, imagine offering these refreshing beverages with a customizable flavor options—and even an optional spiked version! If you already have a Taylor Frozen Beverage machine, you can easily add a Flavorburst option and increase your menu signature and LTO offerings!

With our world-famous Flavorburst system, you can effortlessly create both alcoholic and non-alcoholic frozen beverage favorites. Delight your customers with options like strawberry lemonade, peach iced tea, or mango-infused concoctions, all made possible with just a simple touch of a button. Expand your menu, attract a broader audience, and enhance your beverage offerings this summer with the power of Flavorburst.

Enhance Your Summer with Taylor Products

Stay ahead of the competition by embracing these cutting-edge innovations from Taylor Products. Whether you're looking to streamline your service with the Icetro ISI-271 or captivate your customers with exciting frozen beverage flavors, we’ve got your summer covered.

Contact your Taylor Products representative today to discover how these new solutions can elevate your business this season!

*Not all size cups and cones will work.
